key_components.description: Los 6 componentes clave (KC1–KC6) que componen la arquitectura de un agente de IA, derivados de la Sección 2 'Secure Agentic Architectures' del 'Securing Agentic Applications Guide 1.0'. Cada KC define un bloque constructivo del agente con sus sub-componentes y las amenazas a las que expone directamente.
key_components.pipeline_role: Los KCs se usan como capa de análisis de superficie de ataque: dado un agente con determinados capability_flags, se pueden mapear a los KCs que lo componen y derivar el conjunto de amenazas inherentes a esa combinación.

components.name: Generative Language Models
components.description: The 'brain' (Cognitive engine) of the agent (e.g., GPT-4, Claude), responsible for understanding, reasoning, planning, and generating responses. LLMs are often built on pre-trained foundation models, which provide broad knowledge and can be specialized using techniques like prompt engineering or fine-tuning.

sub_components.name: Large Language Models (LLMs)
sub_components.description: The core cognitive engine utilizing pre-trained foundation models (e.g., GPT series, Claude series, Llama series, Gemini series) for reasoning, planning, and generation, primarily directed via prompt engineering and operating within constraints like context window, latency, and cost.

sub_components.name: Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs)
sub_components.description: LLMs capable of processing and/or generating information across multiple data types beyond text (e.g., images, audio), enabling agents to perform a wider variety of tasks involving visual or auditory information (e.g., GPT-4V, Gemini).

sub_components.name: Small-Language Models (SLMs)
sub_components.description: Language models with fewer parameters, trained on much smaller, more focused datasets. Designed to perform a specific task or work in a particular use case. Characterized by a smaller weight space, parameter size, and context window when compared with LLMs.

sub_components.name: Fine-tuned Models
sub_components.description: Language models (LLMs/MLLMs) that undergo additional training on specific datasets to specialize their capabilities, enhancing performance, adopting personas, or improving reliability for particular tasks, domains, or interaction styles required by the agent.

components.attack_surface_summary: Core vulnerabilities in the 'brain' of the agent: hallucinations, goal misalignment, deceptive reasoning, and manipulating humans. Foundation models generate incorrect information that propagates (T5); attacks target the core decision-making capabilities (T6); model alignment issues lead to unintended behaviors (T7); models exploit human trust to manipulate users (T15).

components.name: Orchestration (Control Flow Mechanisms)
components.description: Dictate the agent's overall behavior, information flow, and decision-making processes. The specific mechanism (e.g., 'sequential' for layered architectures, 'dynamic' for blackboard architectures, or 'coordinated' for multi-agent systems) depends on the architecture and impacts the agent's responsiveness and efficiency.

sub_components.name: Workflows
sub_components.description: A structured, pre-defined sequence of tasks or steps that agents follow to achieve a goal. Workflows define the flow of information and actions within the agent's operation and among agents. They can be linear, conditional, or iterative, depending on the task's complexity.

sub_components.name: Hierarchical Planning
sub_components.description: Multiple agents collaborating via an orchestrator (router). The orchestrator understands the task, decomposes it into sub-tasks, routes to specialized agents, monitors agent performance, and adjusts workflows to optimize efficiency.

sub_components.name: Multi-agent Collaboration
sub_components.description: Multiple agents working together to achieve a common goal. Agents can communicate and coordinate their actions, sharing information and resources. Useful for complex tasks that require diverse skills or knowledge.

components.attack_surface_summary: Vulnerabilities in workflow control: goal manipulation (T6), lack of auditability through workflow (T8), identity confusion especially in multi-agent systems (T9), overwhelming human oversight (T10), corrupting inter-agent messaging (T12), compromising agent orchestration (T13), exploiting trust relationships between agents and workflows (T14).

components.name: Reasoning / Planning Paradigm
components.description: Agents utilize LLMs to solve complex tasks requiring multiple steps using strategic thinking. Agents break down high-level tasks into smaller tasks (steps), each with a different sub-goal.

sub_components.name: Structured Planning / Execution (ReWoo, LLM Compiler, Plan-and-Execute)
sub_components.description: Focuses on decomposing tasks into a formal plan, defining sequences of actions often involving specific tool calls, and executing the plan, sometimes using separate 'planner' and 'executor' components.

sub_components.name: ReAct (Reason + Act)
sub_components.description: Dynamically interleaves reasoning steps with actions (like using tools or querying APIs) and updates reasoning based on feedback.

sub_components.name: Chain of Thought (CoT)
sub_components.description: Enhances reasoning quality by prompting step-by-step 'thinking', inducing an LLM to generate a set of 'thoughts' before arriving at a final action or conclusion.

sub_components.name: Tree of Thoughts (ToT)
sub_components.description: Generalizes CoT by exploring multiple reasoning paths and plans in parallel with lookahead, backtracking, and self-evaluation.

components.attack_surface_summary: Weaknesses in decision processes: cascading hallucinations affecting reasoning quality and propagating through planning steps (T5), direct attacks on the reasoning process to manipulate goals (T6), subtle reasoning misalignments (T7), obscuring decision trails in reasoning chains (T8), leveraging reasoning to craft manipulative responses (T15).

components.name: Memory Modules
components.description: Enable the agent to retain short-term (immediate context) and long-term information (past interactions, knowledge) for coherent and personalized interactions. Context 'sensitivity' (classification or compartmentalization) is used to reduce the risk of unauthorized information exposure. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) used with a vector database is common for long-term memory.

sub_components.name: In agent session memory
sub_components.description: Memory is limited to a single agent and a single session, limiting the ability to compromise additional agents/sessions if compromised.

sub_components.name: Cross-agent session memory
sub_components.description: Memory is shared across multiple agents, but is limited to a single session. A single compromised agent might compromise multiple agents operating at the same session.

sub_components.name: In agent cross-session memory
sub_components.description: Memory is limited to a single agent, but is shared across multiple sessions. One compromised session might cause compromising multiple sessions.

sub_components.name: Cross-agent cross-session memory
sub_components.description: Memory is shared across multiple agents and sessions. If an agent is compromised in a specific session, it might compromise additional sessions and/or agents. Highest risk tier.

sub_components.name: In agent cross-user memory
sub_components.description: Memory is limited to a single agent but is shared across multiple users. A compromised agent might have the ability to compromise multiple users.

sub_components.name: Cross-agent cross-user memory
sub_components.description: Memory is shared across multiple agents and users. A compromised agent might have the ability to compromise additional agents and users. Maximum blast radius.

components.attack_surface_summary: Data integrity issues: memory poisoning directly targeting all memory types KC4.1-KC4.6 (T1), breaking information system boundary through context collapse causing unauthorized data access (T3), storing and amplifying hallucinations across sessions or agents (T5), abusing shared context and breaking integrity (T6), manipulating or erasing evidence from memory (T8), affecting shared memory in multi-agent systems (T12).

components.name: Tool Integration Frameworks
components.description: Allow agents to extend their capabilities beyond text by using external tools (APIs, functions, data stores) to interact with the real world or other systems. Tool integration framework is used to manage the selection and use of these tools.

sub_components.name: Flexible Libraries / SDK Features
sub_components.description: Code-level building blocks (e.g., LangChain, AG2, Agents, CrewAI, MCP) or specific API capabilities for developers. High flexibility and control over agent behavior and tool orchestration, but require more coding effort.

sub_components.name: Managed Platforms / Services
sub_components.description: Vendor-provided solutions (like Amazon Bedrock Agents, Microsoft Copilot Platform) that handle infrastructure, simplify setup, and manage orchestration. Feature easier integration within the provider's ecosystem, trading some flexibility for faster development.

sub_components.name: Managed APIs
sub_components.description: Vendor-hosted services (like OpenAI's Assistants API) providing higher-level abstractions. Manage complexities like state and aspects of tool orchestration via API calls.

components.attack_surface_summary: Tool exploitation vulnerabilities: tool misuse as core vulnerability for all tool integration types, including via MCP (T2), tools often run with specific privileges that can be exploited/excessive agency (T3), interfering with data records or assets within a tool (T6), creating subtle reasoning misalignments (T7), tool use may lack proper logging and auditability (T8), tools might enable unexpected code execution (T11).

components.name: Operational Environment (Agencies)
components.description: Though LLMs are restricted to data available up to their last training update, agents can interface with external environments through tools and function calls. Utilizing different agencies enables interaction with, gathering, and processing of information from external environments.

sub_components.name: API Access
sub_components.description: KC6.1.1 Limited API Access: agent uses LLM to generate parameters to a predefined API call — risk of parameter pollution attacks. KC6.1.2 Extensive API Access: agent uses LLM to generate the entire API call — risk of unauthorized API calls via excessive authorization.

sub_components.name: Code Execution
sub_components.description: KC6.2.1 Limited Code Execution: agent uses LLM to generate parameters to a predefined function — risk of code injection. KC6.2.2 Extensive Code Execution: agent runs code generated by an LLM — risk of arbitrary code execution.

sub_components.name: Database Execution
sub_components.description: KC6.3.1 Limited: limited permission set (read-only or parameterized writes). KC6.3.2 Extensive: full CRUD operations — risk of altering/deleting any record. KC6.3.3 Agent Memory or Context Data Sources (RAG agent): compromised agent might disrupt data or provide malformed retrieved information.

sub_components.name: Web Access Capabilities (web-use)
sub_components.description: Agent utilizing LLM for operating with the browser. Compromised agent is likely to form due to exposure to untrusted web content and might perform unwanted operations via excessive authorization.

sub_components.name: Controlling PC Operations (PC-use)
sub_components.description: Agent utilizing LLM for operating with the operating system, including file system. Compromised agent might perform unwanted operations, expose personal information, and perform malicious operations such as encrypting files.

sub_components.name: Operating Critical Systems (e.g., SCADA)
sub_components.description: Agent using LLM to operate critical systems. Unauthorized operations can lead to catastrophic failures. A compromised agent may cause severe disruptions in system operations.

sub_components.name: Access to IoT Devices
sub_components.description: Unauthorized control over IoT devices. A compromised agent could impact the operational environment hosting such IoT devices, potentially utilizing them in malicious or unintended ways.

components.attack_surface_summary: Monitoring gaps and external system risks: misusing access in all operational environments (T2), privilege compromise highest risk in extensive access environments KC6.1.2 and KC6.2.2 (T3), external services can be overwhelmed (T4), excessive activity requiring human approval (T10), direct risk to code execution environments KC6.2 (T11), using external systems for side channel communications and memory persistence (T12), compromised AI agent activity outside monitoring limits (T13), leveraging operational access to manipulate humans (T15).

architecture_kc_composition.description: Cómo los KCs se combinan en los patrones de arquitectura más comunes.

lifecycle_security.description: Guías de seguridad organizadas por fase del ciclo de vida de desarrollo de agentes, derivadas de la Sección 3 'Agentic Developer Guidelines' del 'Securing Agentic Applications Guide 1.0'. Permite al sistema de validación determinar qué controles aplican según la etapa del agente.

phases.description: Agentic AI systems require more than mitigations to core security risks of LLMs. Persistent memory raises the risk of context poisoning, data leakage, and unauthorized state retention. Autonomous planning opens the door to misaligned objectives, recursive decision loops, and unpredictable emergent behavior. These risks must be accounted for at design time through threat modeling, defining 'safe failure' states, charting integration boundaries, specifying memory access policies, and ensuring human-in-the-loop safeguards.

practices.name: Threat Modeling for Agentic Systems
practices.purpose: Identify and model agentic-specific threats including prompt injection, memory poisoning, tool misuse, and privilege escalation across the agent's planned capabilities.
practices.approach: Use the Taxonomy Navigator (capability_taxonomy) as the threat modeling framework. For each activated step, enumerate the threats_detail and map to activated_risks.

practices.name: System Prompt Engineering & Hardening
practices.purpose: Define the agent's core instructions, capabilities, and limitations securely to prevent manipulation and unintended behavior.
key_actions: Clear Boundaries & Safeguards: Explicitly state DOs and DON'Ts, forbidden topics, operational scope, and ethical guidelines. Prefer predetermined allowable topics with implicit deny policy.
Robustness against Injection: use clear delimiters (XML tags, triple backticks) to separate instructions from user input. Instruct the model to be wary of attempts to override its core instructions.
Role Definition: clearly define the agent's persona and purpose to anchor its behavior.
Iterative Refinement: test prompts against known injection techniques and refine based on results.
Minimal and Focused Fine-Tuning: minimize fine-tuning to meet use case. Benchmark security adherence before and after tuning.

practices.name: Secure Coding Practices
practices.purpose: Implement standard secure coding principles adapted for AI agent development.
key_actions: Input Validation: validate all inputs, not just tool arguments — user prompts, API responses, data retrieved from memory. Use allowlists where possible.
Error Handling: implement robust error handling that avoids leaking sensitive information in error messages.
Secure Key Management: avoid hardcoding secrets. Use environment variables, dependency injection, or dedicated secrets management services.
Least Privilege: ensure components run with the minimum permissions necessary.

practices.name: Content Moderation Integration
practices.purpose: Plan for detecting and filtering harmful or policy-violating content in both inputs and outputs early in the design.
key_actions: Identify necessary checks: hate speech, PII, toxicity, specific disallowed topics.
Evaluate tools: rule-based filters, ML classifiers, and external APIs (Meta's LlamaGuard, AWS Comprehend, Azure Content Safety, OpenAI Moderation API).
Design how moderation results will trigger actions: block, flag, sanitize, alert.
Ensure you test your content moderation against your policies and for correctness.

practices.name: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Design
practices.purpose: Determine where human oversight is critical before the agent takes high-impact actions.
key_actions: Risk-Based Identification: identify actions requiring approval (sending emails, modifying databases, executing code, spending funds, updating critical memory). Use the EU AI Act's list of high-risk actions.
Clear Workflow: design a user-friendly interface for review, approval, or rejection. It should be clear to the user what they are approving. Log the human decision.
Include strong rate limiting to prevent overwhelming humans in a DoS situation.
Framework Integration: leverage built-in HITL features in agent frameworks (Langchain Interrupts, Autogen User_Proxy_Agent, CrewAI Human Input).

practices.name: Memory Security Design
practices.purpose: Plan how to protect the agent's short-term and long-term memory from unauthorized access, tampering, and data leakage.
key_actions: Access Control: use standard mechanisms (IAM roles, API keys, database permissions) to restrict access based on the principle of least privilege.
Strip Dangerous Tokens: remove 'ignore', 'system', or 'from now on' from past messages.
Encryption: encrypt data both at rest and in transit (during retrieval/updates).
Input Validation for Memory: validate and sanitize data before storing to prevent storing malicious content or corrupted data.
PII Handling: design mechanisms for PII detection and redaction/anonymization before storage.
Human in the loop: use human oversight to both approve and audit memory entries.

practices.name: Input/Output Validation & Sanitization Design
practices.purpose: Define strategies to ensure the integrity and safety of data flowing into and out of the agent and its tools. Minimize the data exposed to the LLM.
key_actions: Apply AI Guardrails to both inputs and outputs: integrate AI guardrail code directly into the agent or tool, or allow an AI guardrail to be accessible as a tool, or insert an AI guardrail via a man-in-the-middle approach (e.g., MCP proxy).

Input Sanitization and Escaping: escape or strip special tokens (##, <<, {{}}) before injecting user input into prompts. Avoid prompt templating patterns that concatenate raw user input into instructions.
Schema Enforcement: define strict schemas for tool arguments and expected outputs. Use structured formats like JSON with string parsing.
Allow/Deny Lists: use allow lists for known-good values and deny lists for known-bad patterns.
Output Sanitization Strategy: plan how to neutralize potentially malicious content in LLM outputs before rendering or passing to other systems.
Secure Rendering: use safe methods for displaying agent output in UIs (e.g., element.textContent instead of element.innerHTML).

practices.name: Authorization and Authentication Design
practices.purpose: Authenticate and authorize agentic systems to perform actions and read data on behalf of users or systems.
key_actions: Identify Permission Boundaries: examine agent and tools for expected actions and data reads. Ensure agents and tools are coded to respect their permissions.

Use Identity Providers and Authorization Servers: use existing identity and authorization frameworks. Determine if an agent is acting as a business system or on behalf of a user and create the correct identity type.
Assign Decentralized Identifiers to Agents: make use of DIDs to identify and authenticate remote agents.

phases.description: As organizations move toward productionizing agentic applications, a robust and adaptive development lifecycle becomes essential. Development environments should sandbox agent chains, constrain tool usage, and guard against memory corruption or drift. Deployment pipelines must include snapshotting agent capabilities, logging audit trails, and embedding signed constraints on tool/API usage and memory schema.

practices.name: Static Analysis & Code Scanning (SAST)
practices.purpose: Automatically detect potential security vulnerabilities in the agent's source code before runtime.
key_actions: Integrate SAST tools into the CI/CD pipeline to scan code on commit/merge.
Focus on common web vulnerabilities, insecure use of APIs, hardcoded secrets, and unsafe code patterns.
Tools: Bandit (Python), Semgrep (multi-language), ESLint + security plugins (JavaScript), Meta's PurpleLlama CodeShield (focused on secure code generation).

practices.name: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning (SCA)
practices.purpose: Identify known vulnerabilities in third-party libraries and dependencies used by the agent.
key_actions: Integrate SCA tools into the CI/CD pipeline or use package manager features.
Regularly scan dependencies and update libraries with known vulnerabilities.
Tools: Snyk, GitLab Dependency Scanning, pip-audit, GitHub Dependabot.

practices.name: Environment Hardening & Sandboxing
practices.purpose: Isolate the agent's execution environment to limit the potential impact of a compromise.
key_actions: Restrict the deployment pipeline: prevent access to deployment pipeline and configuration by the agent itself.
Sandboxing options: OS-level Containers (Docker, Podman), VM/MicroVM (Firecracker, QEMU/KVM), WebAssembly (memory safety), Sandboxed Interpreters (Pyodide), Cloud Sandboxing Services.
Filesystem/Network Restrictions: configure strict permissions within the sandbox (read-only filesystem where possible, limited network egress/ingress).
Principle of Least Privilege: run agent processes with minimal OS-level privileges.

practices.name: Secure Configuration Management
practices.purpose: Securely manage configurations, especially secrets and API keys, during deployment.
key_actions: Secrets Management: use dedicated systems (AWS Secrets Manager, Google Secret Manager, Vault) instead of config files or environment variables. Implement credential rotation. Verify that no secrets are ever written into logs.
API Access Control: use fine-grained access controls for external APIs (OAuth2 scopes, restricted API keys) granting only necessary permissions.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Security: scan IaC templates (Terraform, CloudFormation) for security misconfigurations before deployment.

practices.name: Pre-deployment Testing (Fuzzing, Pen Testing)
practices.purpose: Actively probe the agent and its interfaces for vulnerabilities before release.
key_actions: Prompt Interface Fuzzing: use automated tools to send malformed, unexpected, or adversarial inputs to the agent's prompt interface. Tools: PromptFoo, PyRIT, Garak.
API Fuzzing: test any custom APIs exposed by the agent system.
Targeted Penetration Testing: conduct manual or automated penetration tests focusing on risks identified during threat modeling.

practices.name: Runtime Security with Memory Isolation
practices.purpose: Provide defense-in-depth even if the underlying LLM is vulnerable to prompt injection.
key_actions: Incorporate runtime security architectures like Google's CaMeL (Capabilities for Machine Learning).
Explicitly separate control flow generation (Privileged LLM seeing only trusted prompts) from untrusted data processing (Quarantined LLM with no tool access).
Use static APIs/methods or a custom interpreter that enforces security policies based on fine-grained capabilities and data flow tracking before executing tool calls.
Prevent untrusted data from directly influencing the agent's actions or exfiltrating sensitive information via unauthorized tool parameters.

practices.name: Separating Data Planes from Control Planes
practices.purpose: Limit the ability of a single agent compromise to cascade into a systemic failure. Applies to Multi-Agent Architectures.
key_actions: Differentiate between control messages (task assignments, commands) and data messages (shared information) in inter-agent communication.
Control channels require stronger authentication, authorization, and integrity checks to prevent a compromised agent from issuing malicious commands or disrupting coordination.

practices.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) Access and Ephemeral Credentials
practices.purpose: Reduce the window of opportunity for misuse if credentials are compromised.
key_actions: Agents requiring access to sensitive tools or data should operate under the principle of least privilege in time.
Instead of using long-lived static credentials, employ mechanisms that grant access permissions only when needed and for the shortest duration possible.
Use ephemeral credentials: short-lived API tokens (OAuth tokens, signed JWTs) or temporary cloud credentials (AWS STS, GCP IAM credentials) that expire automatically.

phases.description: Live agentic systems require continuous behavioral monitoring that extends far beyond performance metrics. Runtime observability must capture decisions, plan evolution, memory access patterns, and agent-tool interactions. Behavioral drift must trigger alerts or invoke safeguards. Agents should log timestamped reasoning traces for post-incident analysis, and operators must retain real-time override capabilities.

practices.name: Continuous Monitoring & Anomaly Detection
practices.purpose: Detect malicious activity, policy violations, and deviations from expected behavior in real-time.
key_actions: LLM Input/Output Scanning: monitor prompts and responses for jailbreak techniques, policy violations, and PII.
Tool Invocation Monitoring: log all tool calls, parameters, and results. Monitor unusual frequency, suspicious parameter values, or calls to sensitive tools. Implement rate limiting per session/user.
Plan & Execution Monitoring: validate generated plans for coherence, feasibility, safety, and policy alignment before execution. Use rule-based checks or LLM as a Judge.
Memory Anomaly Detection: monitor memory update patterns for unusual frequency, size, or content.
Behavioral Analysis (Multi-Agent): monitor communication patterns and actions between agents for collusion, manipulation, or unexpected emergent behavior.
SIEM Integration: feed logs and alerts into a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system.
Automated Anomaly Response: create automations to immediately address anomalous behavior (compute quarantine, circuit breakers, automated scaling, revoking access to credentials).

practices.name: Runtime Guardrails & Automated Moderation
practices.purpose: Enforce policies and constraints dynamically during agent operation.
key_actions: Input/Output Guardrails: implement real-time checks to block or sanitize inputs/outputs based on predefined rules. Examples: Nemo Guardrails, OpenAI Agents SDK Custom Guardrails.

Locate guardrails at the right layer: API Gateway (Input Layer) for deterministic controls; LLM (Model) for alignment rules; Agent (Reasoning & Tools) for orchestration and tool use guardrails; Output (Post Process) for final output filtering.
Content Filtering (Inter-Agent/Tool): sanitize data exchanged between agents or between agents and tools/APIs. Apply filtering at the orchestrator level or message handoff points.
Memory TTL (time to live) or Expiration: expire old or stale memory content automatically.
Memory Sanitization & PII Redaction: use safe memory wrappers, implement read-only buffers, sanitize and validate data before storing in memory.
Context Window: implement context-window bound with access. Limit how far back a model can recall or query from past conversations.
Content Security Policy (CSP): implement CSP HTTP headers as a defense-in-depth measure in the browser.

practices.name: Logging, Auditing & Traceability
practices.purpose: Support debugging, security analysis, compliance, and understanding agent behavior through detailed records.
key_actions: Centralized Logging & Monitoring Platforms: utilize platforms designed for ML/LLM observability (MLFlow, Langfuse, LangSmith, Cloud provider tools).
Session Scoping: tag memory buffers by session ID or user identity for logging and auditing.
Comprehensive Logging: log agent reasoning steps, generated plans, validation results, tool calls (with parameters/results), HITL interactions, errors, and state changes.
Structured Logging: use formats like JSON for easier automated parsing and analysis.
Traceability: implement trace IDs that propagate through agent steps and tool calls.
Operational security (OpSec): use multi-tenant tagging, implement immutable logs, apply least privilege access to log platforms, maintain audit logs of access to raw logs.
Never log sensitive information: remove, mask, sanitize, hash, or encrypt session tokens, access tokens, PII, authentication passwords, encryption keys, payment data.

practices.name: Vulnerability Scanning (Runtime)
practices.purpose: Continuously scan the running application and environment for new vulnerabilities.
key_actions: Perform periodic infrastructure vulnerability scans.
Integrate findings into a patch management process.
Utilize DAST scanning against lower environments for APIs and other common interfaces (OWASP ZAP).
Use port and CVE scanners for environment endpoints.

practices.name: Incident Response Planning
practices.purpose: Have a predefined plan to handle security incidents involving the AI agent.
key_actions: Define what constitutes an incident: successful prompt injection causing harm, data breach via agent, agent performing unauthorized actions.
Outline steps for containment (disabling the agent, restricting tool access), analysis (using logs and monitoring data), remediation, and reporting.
Assign roles and responsibilities for incident response.
Regularly test the plan using tabletops and 'fire' drills.

practices.name: AI Bot Mitigation and Controls
practices.purpose: Establish verifiable agent identity to allow site owners and other agents to verify who is calling before sharing data or executing actions.
key_actions: Adopt a multi-factor identity bundle: serve from a documented IP range and a verbose User-Agent string (including optional headers: X-AI-Agent, X-AI-Agent-ID/Signature).
Cryptographic request signing: sign every HTTP request with RFC 9421 Message Signatures; expose the verification key at /.well-known/agent-public-key.json.
Agent Name Service (ANS): publish an ANSName that encodes protocol, capability, provider and version; register the name + public key in an open Agent Registry.
Identify transparently: ship the identity bundle on every request. Declare intent, respect policy — advertise purpose via X-Agent-Intent (crawl, pay, assist).

operational_capabilities.description: Capacidades operacionales del agente (KC6.1–KC6.6) derivadas de la Sección 5 'Key Operational Capabilities' del 'Securing Agentic Applications Guide 1.0'. Cada capability mapea a los capability_flags del sistema, especifica las amenazas principales que activa, y los controles necesarios para mitigarlas. Esta sección es el puente directo entre los flags de registro y los controles accionables.
operational_capabilities.pipeline_role: Cuando un agente declara un capability_flag como api_access=true, code_execution=true, etc., el sistema busca en esta sección la entrada correspondiente para determinar las core_threats adicionales y los controles específicos requeridos.

capabilities.name: API Access
capabilities.threat_summary: Unauthorized data access/leakage (T3), API abuse DoS and cost overruns (T4, T2), Compromised keys (T3, T9).

controls.name: Enforce Least Privilege with Fine-Grained OAuth Scopes or Limited API Keys
actions: Define the minimum necessary activities for task completion (e.g., never grant an admin complete access to an agent).
Grant access solely to essential assets with minimal access scope; issue access tokens only to necessary clients/agents.
OAuth 2.0 with specific scopes (Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, cloud provider integrated services).
API Keys: employ provider features to enforce limits (AWS API Gateway restriction to specific API stages/methods).
Cloud IAM: assign specific IAM roles with restricted permissions for agents operating as cloud services.

controls.name: Set up Allow/Deny Lists for APIs
actions: Clearly define authorized domains or URL pathways.
Configure a list of permitted base URLs (Allow-List) or URL patterns. Authenticate target URLs against this list before executing external requests.
Use an outward proxy or API Gateway to permit connections only to pre-approved destinations.
For containerized agents, implement network policies to limit outgoing traffic.

controls.name: Prefer API Templates Over Complete LLM-Generated API Calls
actions: Use prepared templates where LLMs only populate established parameters.
Utilize templating libraries like Jinja2.
Leverage structured output capabilities with strictly defined schemas.
Define parameter types and requirements before sending requests.
Sanitize web-fetched content using tools like DOMPurify.

capabilities.name: Code Execution
capabilities.threat_summary: Arbitrary code execution RCE (T11, T3), Code injection (T11, T2), DoS via resource exhaustion (T4), Leakage of confidential information (T6).

controls.name: Implement Mandatory Sandboxing
actions: OS-level isolation, containers, VMs, WebAssembly, or cloud solutions.
Reference implementations: NVIDIA's WebAssembly Sandboxing, LangChain's E2B Data Analysis.

controls.name: Perform Static Analysis on Agent-Generated Code
actions: Bandit for Python, Semgrep for multi-language analysis, CodeShield for LLM-generated code.

controls.name: Enforce Resource Limitations
actions: Set strict CPU, memory, and execution time limits.
Implement timeouts for all operations.

controls.name: Additional Security Measures
actions: Use code signing or verification when possible.
Implement strict file system and network restrictions.
Use allow-lists for permitted commands.
Require Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) approval for high-risk operations.
Sanitize all executed code output.
Implement runtime monitoring during execution.

capabilities.name: Database Execution (Queries and RAG access)
capabilities.threat_summary: SQL injection (T2), Unauthorized data exposure/modification (T3), RAG data poisoning/sensitive data retrieval (T1, T5, T3).

controls.name: Use Managed Vector Databases with Access Controls
actions: Restrict data ingest to match the access control capability (never ingest data that can't be protected from unauthorized users).
Apply data classification labels to enforce user privilege.
Utilize specialized RBAC RAGs: Elastic RAG, Pinecone with authentication platforms like Clerk, Authorization platforms like Aserto.

controls.name: Implement Query Safety Measures
actions: Use parameterized or template queries/ORMs exclusively. Never construct SQL using string concatenation.
Grant database access via least-privilege user accounts (SELECT only, limited tables, or row/column level security).
Filter/block dangerous SQL keywords (e.g., DROP, TRUNCATE).
Validate all user inputs influencing queries; if possible, derive from controlled channels only vs context window.

controls.name: RAG-Specific Controls
actions: Implement post-retrieval filtering to check for sensitive content (PII) before agent use.
Apply content verification before embedding into vector stores.
Rate-limit retrieval operations.

capabilities.name: Web Use
capabilities.threat_summary: Malicious web content XSS and exploits (T11), Leakage of confidential information (T6), Phishing/deception (T7), Server-Side Request Forgery SSRF (T2, T3), Access to user's browser data (T3).

controls.name: Sandbox Browser Components
actions: Run in tightly controlled environments.
Avoid using extensions or operating directly in the user's browser.

controls.name: Implement URL Security
actions: Use URL filtering with allow lists.
Leverage Secure Web Gateway (SWG) or Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
Perform reputation checks on target domains.
Enforce proper TLS verification.
Detect and block open redirects or excessive redirection chains. Use DNS-based filtering in addition to HTTP-level filtering.

controls.name: Apply Protective Measures
actions: Use network segmentation to prevent access to internal systems (mitigating SSRF).
Throttle web access rate to prevent abuse.
Restrict downloadable file types.
Implement content sanitization before processing.
Inspect embedded/linked content (e.g., iframes, JS-injected sources).

controls.name: Logging and Monitoring
actions: Log all URL accesses and HTTP responses.

capabilities.name: Controlling PC Operations (Filesystem, OS Commands)
capabilities.threat_summary: Unauthorized file access/modification (T3), Arbitrary OS command execution (T11, T3, T2), Lateral movement (T3).

controls.name: Apply Strict Isolation
actions: Use OS-level sandboxing.
Run agents as restricted users with minimal privileges.
Consider dedicated containers or VMs for isolation.

controls.name: Implement Access Controls
actions: Define strict allow/deny lists for permitted OS operations and file paths.
Use virtual filesystem interfaces where appropriate.
Intercept OS command calls to enforce allow-lists.

controls.name: Limit accumulation of sensitive data
actions: To maintain its status, the sandbox should not accumulate data and sessions.

controls.name: Enhance Monitoring and Oversight
actions: Log all OS-level actions performed by the agent.
Consider HITL approval for critical operations.
Implement command validation before execution.

capabilities.name: Operating Critical Systems (e.g., SCADA controls)
capabilities.threat_summary: Catastrophic physical outcomes (T2, T3, T6, T7), Malicious control injection (T2, T6), False data influencing decisions (T1, T5). Maximum risk tier — requires maximum oversight controls.

controls.name: Apply Maximum Isolation
actions: Use air-gapped or highly segmented networks.
Implement physical security measures.

controls.name: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication
actions: Switch to external flow to require MFA for specific sensitive actions where possible — do not use agent to mediate MFA flow or retain privileged session.
Implement mandatory HITL for every critical action, succinct and engaging enough to retain the user's attention each time (excessive/inefficient prompting results in indiscriminate approval).

controls.name: Implement Safety Mechanisms
actions: Default agent permissions to read-only monitoring.
Use anomaly detection tuned to system safety parameters.
Adhere to industrial control security standards.
Ensure physical interlocks and emergency overrides exist.

capabilities.special_note: Agents in this category require maximum oversight controls per Section 5.6. Consider Human-Over-The-Loop (continuous supervision) rather than standard HITL.

verdict_framework.description: Marco para determinar si un agente es apto para producción basado en cobertura de controles y riesgos activados. Esta es la capa de DECISIÓN del sistema: OWASP no define un veredicto de aptitud para producción, por lo que APT/APT_WITH_RESTRICTIONS/NOT_APT y los umbrales de este marco son criterio explícito del sistema, construido sobre los insumos OWASP (riesgos, amenazas, controles). No se debe confundir esta capa con la taxonomía OWASP (que sí es fiel a los documentos fuente).

high_severity_risks.description: ASI considerados de alta severidad para el veredicto. Si un control crítico de alguno de estos ASI no está implementado, el resultado es NOT_APT. Esta lista pertenece a la capa de decisión del sistema (verdict_framework), no a la taxonomía OWASP. El pipeline debe leer esta lista en lugar de hardcodearla.

verdicts.label: Apto para Producción
verdicts.criteria: All critical controls for activated ASI risks are implemented and verified. All activated playbooks have been executed. Red teaming has been conducted for high-severity activated risks. Immutable logging and incident response plan are in place.

verdicts.label: Apto con Restricciones
verdicts.criteria: Core controls are implemented but one or more of the following apply: some non-critical controls are pending; HITL mechanisms are not yet fully implemented for all high-risk actions; red teaming is scheduled but not yet completed; monitoring baselines are being established. Agent can operate in production with defined operational restrictions.

verdicts.label: No Apto para Producción
verdicts.criteria: One or more of the following: critical controls for activated high-severity ASI risks (ASI01, ASI02, ASI03, ASI05, ASI06) are not implemented; no incident response plan exists; no immutable logging is in place; supply chain has unverified components with direct production access; red teaming has revealed unmitigated critical vulnerabilities.

high_risk_business_domains.description: Domains classified as high-risk per EU AI Act Annex. Require Human-Over-The-Loop (continuous supervision) per Section 8 of Securing Guide.
